candidates.name: Ischemic Stroke
support_spans: A 36‐year‐old man of Indian origin presented at 2:30 a.m. with acute right‐sided weakness and three episodes of vomiting
Brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla without hemorrhagic transformation
A diagnosis of ischemic stroke in a 36‐year‐old gentleman with no apparent risk factors was made
candidates.why: The patient presented with acute right‐sided weakness and vomiting, and brain MRI confirmed a recent ischemic infarction.

candidates.name: Cavernoma
support_spans: Noncontrast CT of the head showed no acute pathology but revealed an incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in the left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of a cavernoma
Brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla without hemorrhagic transformation; the small frontal cavernoma was again noted
candidates.why: The patient has a small frontal cavernoma, which is an incidental finding.

candidates.name: Stroke of Unknown Etiology
support_spans: A diagnosis of ischemic stroke in a 36‐year‐old gentleman with no apparent risk factors was made, and further investigations were initiated to look for the cause
candidates.why: The patient has no apparent risk factors for ischemic stroke, and further investigations are needed to determine the cause.

candidates.name: Stroke
support_spans: A 36‐year‐old man of Indian origin presented at 2:30 a.m. with acute right‐sided weakness and three episodes of vomiting
Motor strength was 0/5 in the right upper limb, 3/5 proximally and 2/5 distally in the right lower limb; left‐sided strength was normal
NIH Stroke Scale score was 7
Brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla without hemorrhagic transformation
candidates.why: The patient presented with acute right-sided weakness and vomiting, and brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction.

candidates.name: Cavernoma
support_spans: Noncontrast CT of the head showed no acute pathology but revealed an incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in the left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of a cavernoma
Brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla without hemorrhagic transformation; the small frontal cavernoma was again noted
candidates.why: The patient has a small frontal cavernoma noted on both CT and MRI scans.

candidates.name: Patent Foramen Ovale
support_spans: Transthoracic echocardiography with bubble study was unremarkable
A diagnosis of ischemic stroke in a 36‐year‐old gentleman with no apparent risk factors was made, and further investigations were initiated to look for the cause
contradict_spans: Transthoracic echocardiography with bubble study was unremarkable
candidates.why: The patient has an ischemic stroke with no apparent risk factors, and further investigations are needed to look for the cause, which could include a patent foramen ovale.

candidates.name: Multiple Sclerosis
support_spans: bilateral torsional nystagmus on vertical and horizontal gaze
partial left ptosis
right upper limb motor strength was 0/5
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms such as bilateral torsional nystagmus, partial left ptosis, and significant weakness in the right upper limb could be indicative of a demyelinating disease like Multiple Sclerosis.

candidates.name: Cavernous Angioma
support_spans: incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in the left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of a cavernoma
candidates.why: The presence of a cavernoma, although incidental, could be related to the patient's symptoms, especially considering the recent ischemic infarction.

candidates.name: Stroke due to other determined cause
support_spans: recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla without hemorrhagic transformation
candidates.why: The diagnosis of ischemic stroke is supported by the recent infarction found on brain MRI, but the cause remains to be determined, prompting further investigation.

selector.rationale: The patient presented with acute right-sided weakness and vomiting, and brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla, supporting the diagnosis of ischemic stroke.

rejected.label: Cavernoma
rejected.why: Although a small frontal cavernoma was noted, it is not the primary cause of the patient's symptoms.

rejected.why: This is another term for cavernoma, and the same reasoning applies.

rejected.why: The diagnosis of ischemic stroke is more specific and supported by the evidence.
